bandReport.notes:
Pages p03-p05 carry Q23-Q39 with no gaps. Q40 is printed on p06 and is CLAIMED BY THIS BAND: it is the third item of the Directions set whose block opens in the right column of p05, so band b2 owns it under the set-ownership rule. BAND b3 MUST SKIP Q40 and start at Q41.

Set D38-40 = Q38, Q39, Q40 exactly (the block says "three (03) items"). Q38 and Q39 are on p05, Q40 on p06; the three are contiguous and each carries the identical context including the six-row jail table as a GFM pipe table. Q41 on p06 is an unrelated standalone item (three-digit numbers divisible by 7) and belongs to b3.

Seam before: p02 ends with Q22 complete (all four options printed) and no Directions block open, so Q23 starts cleanly. Seam after: nothing of b2's is truncated -- Q40's four options all sit on p06 above Q41.

Within-page seam worth knowing: on p04 the stem of Q32 ends the LEFT column and its four options are printed at the TOP of the RIGHT column of the same page. Q32 is complete on p04 and is not a cross-page break.

CURRENCY: Q27 and Q32 print the rupee glyph. Written as "Rs." per the brief's currency rule; no LaTeX macro invented.

FIGURES: no question in Q23-Q40 has a printed diagram, so hasFigure is not set anywhere in this band. See the flags on Q36 -- a dispatch note asked for hasFigure there, but the page prints no diagram (verified at 8x); the brief's rule was followed and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved silently.

questions.stem: If the area of a square is \(2401x^4 + 196x^2 + 4\), then what is its side length ?
If \(x\) varies as \(yz\), then \(y\) varies inversely as
If the points \(P\) and \(Q\) represent real numbers \(0.7\overline{3}\) and \(0.5\overline{6}\) on the number line, then what is the distance between \(P\) and \(Q\) ?
What is the point on the \(xy\)-plane satisfying \(5x + 2y = 7xy\) and \(10x + 3y = 8xy\) ?

The price of an article \(X\) increases by 20% every year and price of article \(Y\) increases by 10% every year. In the year 2010, the price of article \(X\) was Rs. 5000 and price of article \(Y\) was Rs. 2000. In which year the difference in their prices exceeded Rs. 5000 for the first time ?
The ratio of speeds of \(X\) and \(Y\) is \(5 : 6\). If \(Y\) allows \(X\) a start of 70 m in a 1.2 km race, then who will win the race and by what distance ?

options.label: D
options.text: The race finishes in a dead heat

questions.stem: A train takes two hours less for a journey of 300 km if its speed is increased by 5 km/hr from its usual speed. What is its usual speed ?
If 6 men and 8 women can do a piece of work in 10 days; and 13 men and 24 women can do the same work in 4 days, then what is the ratio of daily work done by a man to that of a woman ?

Students of a class are made to sit in rows of equal number of chairs. If number of students is increased by 2 in each row, then the number of rows decreases by 3. If number of students is increased by 4 in each row, then the number of rows decreases by 5. What is the number of students in the class ?
A sum was put at simple interest at certain rate for 2 years. Had it been put at 1% higher rate of interest, it would have fetched Rs. 24 more. What is the sum ?

The population of two villages is 1525 and 2600 respectively. If the ratio of male to female population in the first village is \(27 : 34\) and the ratio of male to female population in the second village is \(6 : 7\), then what is the ratio of male to female population of these two villages taken together ?

In a class room the ratio of number of girls to that of boys is \(3 : 4\). The average height of students in the class is 4.6 feet. If the average height of the boys in the class is 4.8 feet, then what is the average height of the girls in the class ?

options.label: B
options.text: More than 4.2 feet but less than 4.3 feet

options.label: C
options.text: More than 4.3 feet but less than 4.4 feet

options.label: D
options.text: More than 4.4 feet but less than 4.5 feet

questions.stem: What is the median of the data 3, 5, 9, 4, 6, 11, 18 ?
In a pi-diagram there are three sectors. If the ratio of the angles of the sectors is \(1 : 2 : 3\), then what is the angle of the largest sector ?
flags: Printed as "pi-diagram"; transcribed as printed. The intended word is almost certainly "pie-diagram", but the stem is left untouched per the transcribe-as-printed rule.

NO FIGURE IS PRINTED for this item -- verified at 8x from the source PDF. The question is entirely verbal (three sector angles in the ratio 1:2:3). hasFigure is therefore NOT set. A dispatch note asked for hasFigure + figureNote here; that would send the crop operator after a diagram that does not exist on the page, so the brief's rule (hasFigure is for questions that depend on a PRINTED diagram) was followed instead.

questions.stem: The maximum marks in a Test are converted from 250 to 50 for the purpose of an Internal Assessment. The highest marks scored were 170 and lowest marks were 70. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum marks scored in the Internal Assessment ?
